songs.name: Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) Jam

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Avalon set with stellar Dark Star and soaring Eleven
ai_show_review.blurb: The first set delivers a blistering Dark Star > Saint Stephen > The Eleven chain, highlighted by Jerry’s searing leads and Phil’s propulsive bass. The second set features an inspired Other One, a wild New Potato Caboose jam, and a haunting Feedback finale. Overall the show is a high‑octane snapshot of late‑1968 Dead chemistry.
ai_show_review.review:
The October 13, 1968 Avalon Ballroom gig captures the Grateful Dead at a creative peak, riding the wave of their psychedelic ascent. The band launches into an incendiary Dark Star that rolls straight into Saint Stephen and then rockets through the rhythmic marvel of The Eleven – Jerry’s guitar is razor‑sharp while Phil locks in with Mickey and Billy to drive the momentum. Death Don’t Have No Mercy follows, giving a soulful blues interlude before the set closes.
The second set opens with the twin Cryptical Envelopment tease that segues into a thunderous drum duo, then bursts into an electrifying Other One. A daring New Potato Caboose jam—though marred by a splice—still showcases the group’s improvisational daring, and the night ends on a space‑filled Feedback that lingers long after the lights fade. Across all six soundboard sources the mix is remarkably clear, making this one of the most accessible high‑energy recordings from the era.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crystal‑clear mix, no dropouts, and the most praised balance of instruments.

key_highlights: Smoking Dark Star that builds into a seamless Saint Stephen > The Eleven transition
Powerful Eleven where drums and bass lock in tightly
Other One extended jam with soaring improvisation
New Potato Caboose provides a wild, if splice‑marred, psychedelic excursion

band_performance.Jerry: Top‑notch guitar work throughout, especially on Dark Star and Death Don’t Have No Mercy; his leads are crisp and full of soul.
band_performance.Phil: Powerful, tightly locked bass that feeds off the drummers and drives the Eleven and other jams with authority.
band_performance.Mickey: Fabulous early‑set drumming that propels Dark Star and Eleven; later drum segment considered less compelling but still solid.
band_performance.Billy: Provides a steady, driving foundation alongside Mickey, keeping the high‑energy flow intact.
